```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Connect to Redshift with a visitor's own OAuth authorization and query with
DBI. This guide uses Microsoft Entra as the external issuer for a deployment
linked to AWS IAM Identity Center.

## Prepare the deployment

Install `odbc` and the AWS Redshift ODBC 2.x driver with
`IdpTokenAuthPlugin` support. Your administrator must configure
[Redshift's IAM Identity Center integration and trusted issuer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/redshift-iam-access-control-idp-connect-oauth.html),
including user mapping and data access.

Create an Entra Web app registration with `http://localhost:8100` as the
redirect URI. Request the resource and delegated scope trusted by the
Redshift deployment. These are deployment-specific; ask the administrator
for their values.

Put your registration's values in a local `.Renviron` file and restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID=your-tenant-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
OAUTHDB_REDSHIFT_RESOURCE=your-redshift-resource
OAUTHDB_REDSHIFT_SCOPE=your-redshift-delegated-scope
```

## A complete app

Save this as `app.R` and replace the example connection settings:

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

client <- oauth_db_microsoft_client(
  tenant_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID"),
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  token_targets = list(redshift = list(
    resource = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_REDSHIFT_RESOURCE"),
    scopes = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_REDSHIFT_SCOPE")
  ))
)

ui <- oauth_ui(fluidPage(
  actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
  actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
  tableOutput("rows")
), id = "auth", client = client)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_redshift(
    auth$connection,
    server = "cluster.example.eu-west-1.redshift.amazonaws.com",
    database = "reporting",
    target = "redshift"
  )
  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT current_user AS database_user")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server, options = list(port = 8100), uiPattern = ".*")
```

Run `shiny::runApp(port = 8100)` in that directory, then open
`http://localhost:8100` and sign in. The output waits for sign-in and clears
when you sign out.

The query shows the database user chosen by the deployment's mapping.
Replace it with a query for a table that user can read.

## Token types and other issuers

The default `token_type = "EXT_JWT"` supplies an external issuer's JWT
access token. For an IAM Identity Center access token, set
`token_type = "ACCESS_TOKEN"` and use a shinyOAuth client configured to
obtain that token. Other external issuers can use their own shinyOAuth
client in place of the Entra example.

The `target = "redshift"` argument selects the named token target in the
example client. Use the name from your client, or `target = NULL` if it
has no named targets. This helper supplies user tokens to the driver;
IAM key and role-based connection flows need a different setup.

## Driver settings

Set `driver` to the installed driver name or path if it differs from
`"Amazon Redshift (x64)"`. You can pass `CaFile` and `LoginTimeout`
through to the driver. The helper configures token authentication and
verified TLS.

Call `con()` before each query. Connections remain open through ordinary
token refresh and close on account changes, sign-out, or session end. For
cached query results, see [Authentication and sessions](authorization.html).
